reading.body:
Every item in this library is free to access, which makes the full range from mathematical foundations to live hardware announcements available without cost or institutional affiliation.

The seven entries span three distinct layers of knowledge. Two are university course sequences, Stanford CS229 and MIT 6.S191, covering the mathematical and algorithmic ground that the field builds on. Two come from individual educators, Grant Sanderson and Andrej Karpathy, whose single videos and series have become reference points precisely because they explain concepts that formal curricula often leave implicit. The remaining three are event archives from Google, NVIDIA, and the AI Engineer conference, where product announcements and practitioner techniques appear before they reach textbooks. Together they trace a path from first principles through to the hardware roadmap that determines what models can actually be built.

The NVIDIA GTC keynote is the entry most directly connected to compute and power infrastructure, since it is the event where GPU generations and data center capabilities are publicly announced. The others sit further upstream, concerned with how models work rather than what it takes to run them at scale. The data does not cover reading material, benchmarks, or research papers, and it does not say anything about how often the video content is updated between the verified date and any given reader's visit.
